what: Access and Process LOBSTER High-Frequency Data
title: Access and Process LOBSTER High-Frequency Data
text: lobsteR provides tidy workflow requesting, downloading, reading LOBSTER high-frequency order book data directly R. LOBSTER reconstructs full limit order books NASDAQ historical message data delivers pairs message files order book snapshot files. package handles end--end pipeline — authentication, request submission, archive retrieval, file download — can focus analysis. downstream high-frequency econometrics, see highfrequency package. Prerequisites: active account lobsterdata.com required request download data.

title: Access and Process LOBSTER High-Frequency Data
text: lobster_clean() reads one day’s message order book files, keeps continuous trading returns one row per message book state : midquote, spread, depth within given distances best price, sign trade. lobster_snapshots() aggregates regular grid (default 5 seconds). lobster_process() , also straight downloaded .7z archive, without unpacking : snapshot labelled end interval holds midquote instant; time-weighted spread depth; signed volume (shares, net buyer-initiated), trading volume midpoint volume (USD); number messages trades; flags halts depth may cut short number levels file. Time stamps New York time. main choices: Continuous trading runs opening cross (09:30) 16:00 closing cross. Set trading_hours = c("09:30", "13:00") early-close days. crosses reported, never mixed snapshots. Hidden executions signed midquote just trade. exactly midquote (midpoint orders) stay unsigned: count trading_volume midpoint_volume, signed_volume. Depth measured best price side. Depth within bp basis points needs bp / 10000 * price / tick + 1 levels; SPY USD 520 5 bp 27 levels. depth5_truncated shows file . functions read order book block block deep needed, memory use grow number levels: 50-level SPY day (7.2 million messages, 8.7 GB order book CSV) takes minute 4 GB RAM Raspberry Pi 5, read straight archive. polars version functions output python/lobster_clean.py.
code: days <- lobster_archive_files("data-lobster/MSFT_2023-01-03_2023-01-13_10.7z")  snapshots <- lobster_process(   archive  = "data-lobster/MSFT_2023-01-03_2023-01-13_10.7z",   date     = "2023-01-03",   freq     = 5,          # seconds   depth_bp = c(0, 5)     # depth at the best price and within 5 bp of it )  lobster_crosses(snapshots) # opening and closing crosses: price and volume lobster_halts(snapshots)   # trading halts lobster_log(snapshots)     # messages dropped and kept

title: Clean one day of LOBSTER data — lobster_clean
text: message_file, orderbook_file character(1) day's message file order book file: paths CSV files (also .csv.gz), member names inside archive. order book can also parquet file whose columns follow LOBSTER's order (needs 'nanoparquet' package). archive character(1) NULL Path LOBSTER .7z archive holds two files. streamed archive; nothing unpacked disk. 7z program used installed (faster), 'archive' package otherwise; set options(lobsteR.use_7z = FALSE) always use 'archive'. ticker, date Ticker trading day. default parsed file names. trading_hours character(2) numeric(2) Start end continuous session New York time, "HH:MM", "HH:MM:SS" seconds midnight. Defaults 09:30–16:00; use c("09:30", "13:00") early-close days wider window pre- post-market trading (together cut_at_crosses = FALSE). depth_bp numeric Distances best price, basis points, depth computed. 0 gives size best price. NULL reads best level. cut_at_crosses logical(1) Start continuous trading opening cross end closing cross fall inside trading_hours. block_size numeric(1) Bytes CSV text parsed time. block passes one temporary file tempdir(), overwritten block block removed end. Larger blocks slightly faster use memory.

title: Clean one day of LOBSTER data — lobster_clean
text: data.table one row per message continuous trading (types 1 5) columns ts seconds midnight, New York time, LOBSTER. time instant POSIXct America/New_York. type, order_id, size, direction message file. price message price USD. trade_sign +1 buyer-, -1 seller-initiated, 0 unsigned; NA messages executions. midpoint TRUE hidden executions exactly midquote trade. best_ask, best_bid, midquote USD, message. spread quoted spread basis points midquote. depth{bp}_ask, depth{bp}_bid shares within bp basis points best price, value depth_bp. depth{bp}_truncated positive bp: depth may cut short number levels file. Midquote spread NA book crossed one side empty. Depth NA crossed books; empty side depth 0. attribute "lobster" holds day's metadata, crosses, halts, book states session boundaries log dropped messages; lobster_snapshots() needs , lobster_crosses(), lobster_halts() lobster_log() read .

title: Clean one day of LOBSTER data — lobster_clean
text: Book state. Prices stay LOBSTER's integer units (USD x 10000) comparisons. Dummy prices (ask 9999999999, bid -9999999999) mark empty levels. book state valid sides non-empty best ask best bid; otherwise midquote spread NA. one-sided book empty side depth 0; crossed book book variables NA. Depth. distance depth_bp, number shares levels priced within many basis points best price side (midquote). depth0 size best price. depth{bp}_truncated flags rows deepest level file still lies inside distance, depth may cut short number levels requested LOBSTER. Trading hours crosses. Messages outside trading_hours (New York time) dropped. cut_at_crosses = TRUE, continuous trading starts opening cross (type 6, order id -1) ends closing cross (type 6, order id -2) whenever lie inside trading hours. crosses reported, price volume, lobster_crosses(), never enter cleaned messages. Halts. Type 7 messages paired price field: halt (price -1) lasts next resumption trading (price 1) next execution, whichever comes first (files hold halt messages without resumption days trade normally); resumption quoting (price 0) end . Halts found full message stream time filter, halt starts open still ends resumption. halt without resumption lasts close. Messages halts dropped; halts listed lobster_halts(). Trade direction. trade_sign +1 buyer-initiated -1 seller-initiated trades. Visible executions (type 4) take opposite LOBSTER's direction, side resting order. Hidden executions (type 5) carry usable direction NASDAQ feed, signed midquote just trade: book state previous message full stream, compared integer units (2 * price ask + bid). Hidden trades exactly midquote (typically midpoint-peg orders) get trade_sign = 0 midpoint = TRUE; hidden trades without valid quote also get 0.

title: Create a LOBSTER data request (one row per trading day) — request_query
code: # Single symbol, one-week range (weekends and holidays removed automatically) request_query("AAPL", "2023-01-02", "2023-01-06", level = 1) #>   symbol start_date   end_date level #> 2   AAPL 2023-01-03 2023-01-03     1 #> 3   AAPL 2023-01-04 2023-01-04     1 #> 4   AAPL 2023-01-05 2023-01-05     1 #> 5   AAPL 2023-01-06 2023-01-06     1  # Multiple symbols with paired date ranges request_query(   symbol     = c("AAPL", "MSFT"),   start_date = c("2023-01-03", "2023-02-01"),   end_date   = c("2023-01-05", "2023-02-03"),   level      = 1 ) #>   symbol start_date   end_date level #> 1   AAPL 2023-01-03 2023-01-03     1 #> 2   AAPL 2023-01-04 2023-01-04     1 #> 3   AAPL 2023-01-05 2023-01-05     1 #> 4   MSFT 2023-02-01 2023-02-01     1 #> 5   MSFT 2023-02-02 2023-02-02     1 #> 6   MSFT 2023-02-03 2023-02-03     1  # Monthly frequency for a large date range (no per-day expansion) request_query(   symbol     = "SPY",   start_date = "2022-01-01",   end_date   = "2022-12-31",   level      = 10,   frequency  = "1 month" ) #>    symbol start_date   end_date level #> 1     SPY 2022-01-01 2022-01-31    10 #> 2     SPY 2022-02-01 2022-02-28    10 #> 3     SPY 2022-03-01 2022-03-31    10 #> 4     SPY 2022-04-01 2022-04-30    10 #> 5     SPY 2022-05-01 2022-05-31    10 #> 6     SPY 2022-06-01 2022-06-30    10 #> 7     SPY 2022-07-01 2022-07-31    10 #> 8     SPY 2022-08-01 2022-08-31    10 #> 9     SPY 2022-09-01 2022-09-30    10 #> 10    SPY 2022-10-01 2022-10-31    10 #> 11    SPY 2022-11-01 2022-11-30    10 #> 12    SPY 2022-12-01 2022-12-31    10  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Exclude days already in the archive to avoid duplicate requests acct    <- account_login(Sys.getenv("LOBSTER_USER"), Sys.getenv("LOBSTER_PWD")) archive <- account_archive(acct)  req <- request_query(   symbol          = "AAPL",   start_date      = "2023-01-02",   end_date        = "2023-01-31",   level           = 1,   account_archive = archive ) } # }

text: account_login list Output account_login() contains successful authenticated session (valid == TRUE) submission response required navigation. request data.frame tibble returned request_query() columns: symbol, start_date, end_date, level. preopen logical(1) TRUE, ask pre-market messages (LOBSTER's "preopen" option). title: Submit one or more requests to an authenticated LOBSTER account — request_submit
text: Invisibly returns NULL. primary effect queue requests LOBSTER server; processing happens server-side may take time. Use account_archive() afterwards check files become available.

title: Submit one or more requests to an authenticated LOBSTER account — request_submit
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ acct <- account_login(   login = Sys.getenv("LOBSTER_USER"),   pwd   = Sys.getenv("LOBSTER_PWD") )  # Build a request and submit it req <- request_query("AAPL", "2023-01-03", "2023-01-05", level = 1) request_submit(acct, req)  # LOBSTER processes the request server-side; this may take several minutes. # Once done, the files appear in the account archive. archive <- account_archive(acct) } # }
